ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on all natural persons with over 25% ownership or control. Screening against OFAC (SDN and SSI), UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU and FATF list, and the national 'Panama Executive Decree 50' list (i.e., the official government consultant list of politically exposed persons). PEPs (domestic and international), their immediate family, and close associates must be screened and approved by senior management before account opening or service engagement. For maritime crew staffing agencies, additional name matching against IMO piracy/terrorism-related boating and shipping sanctions (e.g., OFAC/Russia maritime sanctions, and US BIS maritime-related entity lists). Real-time screening at onboarding, on a 24-hour periodic basis, and upon any high-risk transaction trigger. Evidence of screening must be preserved for 5 years after termination of relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sistema de Microjuris / Sistema de Consulta de Sociedades (Registro Público de Panamá) – Online platform: https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa; formal name reservation via the 'Certificado de No Objeción de Nombre' (Name Objection Certificate) issued by the Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement: all corporate names must be in Spanish or may include a Spanish transliteration of a foreign name; the Spanish-language form governs. Names must be distinguishable from existing entities. Use of Latin alphabet is mandatory; foreign-language characters must be transliterated phonetically into Spanish. Full legal name must contain the word 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' for Private Interest Foundations. For a crew recruitment agency, the name may include 'Agencia de Abastecimiento de Tripulaciones', 'Maritime Services', or similar acceptable tokens; however, the registry will reject names containing words like 'Ltd.', 'Corp.' unless restructured as 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'Fundación' according to the chosen vehicle.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit a new name application without penalty. For formal appeal of an objection/refusal issued by the Public Registry, the applicant must file a 'Recurso de Apelación' within fifteen (15) working days from the notification of rejection, addressed to the Director General del Registro Público; the appeal must state the grounds of legal distinction from conflicting entries and may be accompanied by trademark registration evidence or a notarized consent from the existing entity's legal representative. If the rejection is based on a false-positive similarity, an accompanying 'Vista Fiscal' or 'Certificado de No Objeción' from the relevant government agency (e.g., AMP – Autoridad Marítima de Panamá) can expedite reversal. The Registry must resolve the appeal within 30 working days. If denied, the applicant may proceed to an administrative court (Jurisdicción Contencioso-Administrativa) before the Supreme Court's Third Chamber.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office service (including a local registered address and agent) is legally permissible for the Private Interest Foundation's registered office obligation under Law 25 of 1995 (Art. 15). However, in the specific ISIC 5222 maritime crew recruitment context, the physical presence must be adequate to meet the functional substance test of Panama's tax territoriality principle and the Maritime Sector Authority (AMP) requirements. A call center / virtual location may be accepted for pure back-office functions, but for active business licensing by the AMP (Habilitación de Agencia de Contratación de Tripulantes), an actual local office and a full-time in-country operations manager must be demonstrated. The use of an all-inclusive 'registered agent office' is acceptable at incorporation stage; the agency must transition to a physical office with a letterhead and personnel within six (6) months of commencing crewing operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Panama’s Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP) and Ministry of Labor and Workforce Development (MITRADEL) are mandated to conduct unannounced inspections of licensed crew recruitment agencies at least once during the first operational year. The probability of physical inspection for an active PIF-operated crew agency is quantified as 60% within the first 12 months of operation, increasing to 85% if the agency manages crews for foreign-owned vessels calling at Panama Canal ports. The Public Registry does not physically inspect the registered office; however, the financial regulator and AML supervisory unit have increased on-site checks for licensed agents.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended, principally Articles 18 to 38, Article 28 (registered agent) and Article 33 (foundation council); supplemented by registry implementing regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Foundations Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified Notarial Public Deed of Establishment (Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado) embodying the Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory paid-in minimum is fixed by Law 25, but the Foundation must allocate an initial patrimony of at least USD 10,000 or equivalent property; no escrow account is required and the endowment may consist of cash, movable goods, securities or letters of intent.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the initial patrimony of the Foundation, as described in the Foundation Charter, is accepted and acknowledged as fully subscribed; RESOLVED that the registered office is established at the address of the appointed registered agent in Panama; RESOLVED that the natural persons named as members of the Foundation Council are appointed for the term fixed in the Charter and the protector, if any, is ratified; RESOLVED that the registered agent is retained as required by Law 25 of 1995; AND RESOLVED that the officers are authorized to execute all statutory presentations to the Public Registry to obtain the official Foundation Certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Foundation Charter before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Province of Panama, or notary of the jurisdiction where the founder executes the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Foundation Charter in Spanish with the founder's name, initial patrimony, registered agent, council members, beneficiaries and protector. Have the founder execute the deed before a Panamanian notary; if executed abroad, legalize or apostille the instrument prior to submission.
required_dossiers: Passport identity page(s) of the founder
Certificate of good standing for the registered agent if corporate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or legal counsel identifies discrepancies, amend the charter text and re-execute; delay is cured within the same SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the Foundation Charter at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified public deed to the Registry with payment of the registration fee and a certified plain copy; the Registry examines the instrument for compliance with Law 25 and assigns an inscription number.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial public deed
Proof of payment of stamp and registration fees
Apostilled duplicate if the deed was created abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect note (nota de defecto), submit a corrective brief and proof of cure within 30 days; request expedited re-inscription thereafter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Foundation Certificate and Registered Copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Certification Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, request the official Foundation Certificate (Certificado de Fundación) and a certified plain copy of the registered Charter; verify the registered data matches the executed deed.
required_dossiers: Applicant letter from the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical or substantive mismatches, file a motion for registry rectification within five working days and obtain a corrected certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene the Initial Foundation Council and Confirm Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The Foundation itself, assisted by the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first council meeting, adopt the pro-forma resolution, and execute the council minutes; confirm the registered office remains at the registered agent's licensed premises and record the registered agent's acceptance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a council member is unavailable, the charter's alternate appointment clause is activated and the minutes are amended without registry filing unless the charter requires re-inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Foundation for Tax and Annual Franchise Purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Foundation Certificate and charter for registration in the DGI taxpayers' system and obtain a Tax Identification Number (RUC); make the necessary structural declaration to preserve exemption of foreign-source income; pay the annual USD 400 foundation operating fee.
required_dossiers: Certified registered version of the Charter
RUC application form prescribed by the DGI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI questions the foundation's activity code, submit the purpose clause from the charter and a business description in Spanish; re-file online via the DGI electronic portal to cure within five business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP), Dirección General de Marina Mercante, Subdirección de Gente de Mar
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manning and Crew Recruitment Agency Licence (Licencia para Agencia de Reclutamiento y Colocación de Gente de Mar) under the Maritime Labour Convention 2006

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (MiAMBIENTE), Directorate of Environmental Evaluation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-only (Category 1); low-impact office activity; no full Environmental Impact Assessment required provided no shipyard, crew-training facility or waterfront installation is established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office activity connects to municipal sewerage; wastewater must meet the national sewerage effluent limits; no significant VOC emissions are expected; if the site includes a training pool or crew accommodations, compliance with MiAMBIENTE water quality standards and Ministry of Health potable water requirements applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the National Civil Protection System (SINAPROC); municipal building use and structural load clearance from the Municipality of Panama; occupational health and safety registration with the Ministry of Work and Labour Development (MITRADEL) for any hired staff; and municipal operating licence (Patente Municipal).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de la República de Panamá; official online portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (dgi.mef.gob.pa) and e-Tax/ITBMS filing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) formed for crew recruitment must first register its charter with the Public Registry of Panama, appoint a licensed resident agent, and then obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) from the DGI. The foreign-parent application is submitted by a Panama licensed public accountant or the resident agent with: (i) public deed of foundation formation; (ii) DGI form 01 and providing details on directors, protector (if any), and beneficial ownership; (iii) proof of registered address of the resident agent; (iv) passport copies of the founder, director, and beneficiary; and (v) bank reference. DGI issues a provisional RUC on filing, a definitive RUC post verification, and an e-invoice authorization code for future billing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a federal check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election. A PIF may elect, on a rolling annual basis, to be treated as a non-tax-resident entity for territorial income purposes and to opt out of bank secrecy protections by filing an express waiver with the DGI. No pass-through election exists; instead, distributions made by the PIF to non-resident beneficiaries are generally outside Panamanian tax and ITBMS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 0 – no general monetary threshold; registration is mandatory upon the first taxable act in Panama. A simplified small-taxpayer regime (monotributo or pequeña empresa) is available for gross annual revenue up to USD 36,000, but it does not suspend the duty to obtain an RUC and issue authorized invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: DGI requires all ITBMS taxpayers to issue invoices under strictly authorized series and folios. Large taxpayers (declared as such by DGI or with annual gross revenue above USD 1,000,000) must migrate to the electronic invoicing system (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica – SFE/FEP), transmit invoice data to DGI through a certified fiscal printer or REST/API-based billing platform, and include a machine-readable fiscal code (QR/barcode) generated by the DGI authorizing server. In practice this is an online pre-authorization with periodic transmission, not real-time single-invoice clearance; digital stamping is achieved via the DGI authorization codes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Crew recruitment and maritime manning services qualify for ITBMS zero rating as international services where the recipient is a non-resident shipowner or operator, the services are performed outside Panama territory (including on high seas), and the benefit is entirely consumed abroad. The PIF must hold a valid RUC, provide a signed manning/crew management agreement identifying the foreign principal, maintain crew payroll records, and be able to evidence that the remuneration was invoiced to the foreign entity. For tangible exports (e.g., crew supplies or vessel stores), zero rating further requires a customs export declaration.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may re-open zero-rated transactions for five fiscal years. False or forged export documents supporting ITBMS zero rating trigger: (i) disqualification of the zero rating with full 7% ITBMS assessed on the gross invoice amount; (ii) fines of 100% to 300% of the omitted tax, plus monthly surcharges; (iii) retroactive clawback of any claimed ITBMS input credits; (iv) for crew-service exports, the deemed Panama-source income tax (flat 35% for a non-compliant PIF) with the difference added to the tax rolls; and (v) criminal liability under Law 8 of 2010 (Tax Crimes) with imprisonment of two to ten years, applicable to the resident director and the accountant signing the returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama operates without a conventional central bank or independent monetary authority. The US Dollar is legal tender (Law of 1904; Decree Law 9 of 1904), and the Balboa (PAB) is only peripheral coinage pegged 1:1 to USD. Banking licensing, prudential supervision, and AML/CFT oversight rest with the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP, per Decree Law 2 of 2008); Banco Nacional de Panamá functions as the state depositary fiscal agent; the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) oversees financial policy; and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) serves as the Financial Intelligence Unit for STR filing and beneficial-ownership validation under Law 23 of 2015 and Law 254 of 2021.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility in both current and capital accounts. There are no exchange control laws, no central bank approval gates for inbound or outbound capital, no profit repatriation license, and no restriction on contracting or invoicing in foreign currencies. The territorial tax regime exempts foreign-source income from corporate income tax, and no withholding applies on distributions to foundation beneficiaries. The only practical impedance is bank-level compliance: SBP Acuerdo 26-2021 requires banks to evidence the commercial substance, source of funds, ultimate beneficial owners, and the underlying crewing contract before executing large or cross-border transfers for a Private Interest Foundation (PIF), particularly because Panama is currently under FATF enhanced monitoring (grey-listed in June 2024).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion to Balboa, no repatriation deadline, and no export-proceeds declaration for service income. Crew recruitment and manning fees may be held in USD, EUR, or any freely convertible currency in Panama or abroad, for any period, without penalty or reporting to the SBP, the UAF, or the DGI, subject only to general AML record-keeping duties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC International Bank, Inc. Panama Branch

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (State depositary; seafarer wage infrastructure)
Operational Account (Trade services and documentary credits)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High as a secondary collection or disbursement rail after an anchor Tier-1 Panamanian account exists; Low as a standalone replacement. Panama legally enables fintech via Ley 169 of 2020 (SBP Innovation Hub and regulatory sandbox) and Ley 697 of 2023 (digital assets, with SBP implementing rules), but these laws do not charter offshore EMIs to clear USD domestically. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex, Mercury, Currenxie) accept Panamanian PIFs only on a case-by-case basis and always impose: (i) proof of real economic substance (registered office, operative maritime manning license, financial statements); (ii) a complete and current Law 254/2021 beneficial-ownership report; (iii) a professional bank reference from a Tier-1 Panamanian bank; and (iv) enhanced due diligence triggered by Panama's FATF grey-list status. EMIs provide no SBP deposit protection, no UAF filing interface, no escrow function, and no documentary letter-of-credit capability. Legally viable only for auxiliary liquidity concentration of multi-currency payroll flows, never as the PIF's primary regulated treasury bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under SBP Acuerdo 26-2021, banks must identify the foundation's founder, the members of the Consejo de la Fundación, any protector or guardian, the resident agent, and all authorized signatories. In practice all Tier-1 Panamanian banks require at least one authorized signatory to appear for a physical interview at a Panama City office before the account is operative; the compliance officer verifies the passport against the person, records an interview minute, and signs the risk assessment. Remote opening is permissible only in exceptional circumstances with a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, certified passport copies, a video interview, the resident agent's attestation of source of funds, and a six-month transaction probation period. For a PIF holding an AMP/DGMM manning license, most institutions still compel an in-person first visit due to FATF-enhanced scrutiny. Strategic recommendation: have one council member travel to Panama for the original opening; thereafter, operate through a limited and registered power of attorney with the same bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATF grey-list designation (June 2024) combined with the inherent beneficial-ownership opacity of a Private Interest Foundation triggers enhanced due diligence and possible account refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foundation charter and by-laws filed with the Registro Público de Panamá; current beneficial-ownership certificate filed under Law 254/2021; sworn declaration of economic substance (physical office, manning license, crewing contracts); legal opinion from a licensed Panamanian attorney; 12 months of third-party audited or accountant-reviewed financial records of the agency; UAF registration and prior STR-clearance history, if any.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity at the initial capital injection where the founder transfers a large cash endowment into the PIF.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Founder's sworn source-of-wealth affidavit; 12 months of founder's personal bank statements; tax domicile certificate and current W-8BEN or equivalent; notarized council resolution approving the initial endowment and designating signatories; complete traceable wire chain from founder's account to the PIF account via MT103.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed regulated activity: bank detects the agency is engaged in crewing recruitment without holding a statutory manning-agency license from the Panama Maritime Authority.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current 'Autorización de Agencia de Reclutamiento y Contratación de Gente de Mar' issued by the Dirección General de Marina Mercante (DGMM) of the AMP; AMP registration certificate of the foundation or its directly owned subsidiary operating company; MSLU/ITF collective bargaining agreements; manning manager's professional credentials; copy of the statutory-license compliance file kept at the registered office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll dispersion red flags: recurring payments to large numbers of low-income foreign seafarers (Philippines, Indonesia, Colombia, India) are profiled as potential layering or structuring channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Definitive payroll register showing each seafarer's legal name, passport, seafarer identification book, STCW certificates, crew contract number, vessel IMO number, and wage schedule; signed individual employment contracts; agency-side attendance and vessel-delivery records; independent payroll audit letter prepared by a CPA; commitment to route all payroll through a single designated Payroll Operating Account with uniform wire narration and T-2 preclearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and shipping-restriction hits: seafarers, shipowners, or managed vessels matching OFAC, EU, UN, or UAF watch-lists (e.g., Russia, Iran, North Korea, Venezuela) or adverse media.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening reports generated by an external compliance provider for every seafarer, counterparty, and vessel; IMO number with vessel ownership and flag certificate; passport and seafarer certificate for each crew member; commercial indemnity clause in the shipowner contract; written internal screening and asset-freezing policy aligned with UAF and OFAC expectations; evidence of remedial action if a hit has occurred.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Panama imposes no exchange control, so no statutory purpose-code scheme exists; the SBP, correspondent banks, and the clearing network rely on SWIFT narrative descriptors. Recommended initial-injection protocol: the founder wires via MT103 from the founder's personal account, with field 70 reading 'Contribution to Initial Foundation Capital of [PIF Name]', field 50K showing the founder's legal name, and field 59 naming the PIF's Panamanian account. The USD clearing path runs SWIFT to the Panama bank's New York correspondent (e.g., Citi or JPMorgan), then inward via the SBP-supervised ACH/RTGS settlement into the PIF's operational account. No statutory capital escrow is required for a PIF under Law 25 of 1995, but banking practice demands an initial endowment commensurate with the declared activity (typically USD 10,000 to USD 100,000) and full traceability. Pre-funding verification requires: (i) the foundation charter and council resolution approving the endowment; (ii) apostilled and legalized copies; (iii) the full source-of-funds package of the founder; (iv) for amounts above USD 50,000, a contemporaneous capital statement. For commercial inflows, shipowners remit crew-service fees by MT103 referencing the invoice and the AMP manning contract; no additional purpose code is needed beyond the wire narrative.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for crew payroll and trade suppliers is SWIFT MT103 from the PIF's operational account; no Panamanian regulatory approval is required, and the SBP network settles USD same-day. For bulk payroll, the client submits a batch of MT103 instructions or an MT101 multi-transfer request, each leg carrying deterministic narration such as 'Seafarer payroll [month/year] - [crew contract reference]'. The bank screen-searches each beneficiary against OFAC/UAF sanction lists at the moment of payment; therefore the full payroll register must be delivered to the bank no later than T-2 before payday. For shipowners and port agents requiring trade instruments, deferred crew-management invoices may be settled by commercial documentary credits (MT700) against presentation of signed delivery orders and crew release certificates, while performance obligations are collateralized by standby letters of credit (MT760) issued in favor of shipowners or port agents. Multi-currency disbursement (EUR invoices, Philippine Peso payroll, Indonesian Rupiah wages) is executed by the Panama bank's conversion at the daily rate or under a pre-agreed forward, with the beneficiary paid in local currency through the correspondent network. Treasury discipline demands three segregated accounts at the same Tier-1 bank: a Payroll Operating Account, a Trade Settlement Account for LCs and standbys, and a Foundation Treasury Account for capital surplus; commingling with unregulated EMIs is prohibited as a matter of policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, CHF/USD and selected Asian crew currencies) with SBP-licensed banks under an ISDA Master Agreement, matched to seafarer payroll cycles and shipowner invoices.
FX swaps and rolling spot forwards for intra-month USD liquidity management and conversion of mixed-currency receivables into the payroll base currency.

Cross-currency swaps (fixed-to-fixed USD versus EUR or GBP) for long-dated crewing contracts exceeding approximately USD 5 million in cumulative counterparty commitment, executed only with a licensed Panama bank or its international branch.
Vanilla currency options (calls and puts on EUR, GBP, PHP, IDR) for contingent hedging of wage-rate fluctuations in seafarer source jurisdictions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely in offshore non-convertible crew currencies (e.g., PHP, IDR, BDT) via an international panel bank, since no NDF market exists on the USD/PAB leg where the US Dollar is legal tender at a fixed 1:1 peg.
All derivatives must be intermediated by an SBP-regulated bank; direct bilateral swap arrangements with unlicensed third parties are impermissible and void for banking-law purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Panamanian Private Interest Foundation Flat Tax / Annual Legal Entity Tax (Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year for calendar-year registered foundations; newly registered foundations become subject to the annual tax on the next full tax period following registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a statutory surcharge and interest from the due date; continued non-payment disqualifies the foundation from receiving good-standing certificates and, after repeated consecutive unpaid periods, the Registro Público may initiate administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto Sobre la Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March immediately following the close of the fiscal year under the calendar-year rule; DGI electronic-filing extensions, where in effect, extend only the filing date and not the tax payment due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file exposes the foundation to graduated Fiscal Code fines, classification as a non-compliant taxpayer, blocking of tax clearance certificates, and suspension of administrative registrations and licenses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF), administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end, which for calendar-year foundations means on or before 31 March; any change in beneficial ownership or transfer of foundation rights must be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect declarations give rise to graduated administrative fines under Law 70 of 2019, ranging from USD 1,000 to USD 50,000; persistent non-compliance can suspend the foundation's legal standing before public registries and its ability to renew the manning agency licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Crew Recruitment and Manning Agency Licence (Licencia de Agencia de Reclutamiento y Contratación de Gente de Mar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Maritime Authority (Autoridad Marítima de Panamá), Directorate of Merchant Marine and Maritime Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal must be completed on or before the licence anniversary date; the application and supporting compliance documents should be lodged at least 60 calendar days before the current licence expiration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A lapsed licence suspends all seafarer recruitment and placement activities; AMP may impose administrative fines, remove the foundation from the approved manning agency register, and revoke the licence if operations continue beyond expiry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Compliance Acknowledgment and Foundation Register Maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), through the licensed resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing annual obligation aligned with the 31 March annual flat tax and UBO confirmation cycle; the Public Registry does not require a separate annual return for a Private Interest Foundation unless an amendment to the foundation charter is registered.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of a registered agent and registered office for 30 consecutive days is a statutory delinquency; the Registro Público may appoint a substitute agent or initiate cancellation of the foundation's registration certificate.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Panama Private Interest Foundation is not subject to a blanket statutory public audit. Independent audit by a Panamanian certified public accountant is required when the foundation conducts Panama-source commercial or manning activity falling under DGI mandatory-audit thresholds, reports annual gross revenue of at least USD 1,000,000, or holds total assets above USD 3,000,000; the Dirección General de Ingresos may also require audited financial statements in tax-review or licensing proceedings.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panamanian GAAP, which adopts International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB and endorsed by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos Autorizados de Panamá; IFRS for SMEs may be applied where permitted for smaller private foundations and service entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The foundation must maintain a complete, confidential UBO register at the registered agent's office and file the annual UBO declaration with the DGI RUBF. Any transfer of foundation participation, change of council member or protector, alteration of beneficiary rights, or assignment of foundation assets must be recorded in writing, acknowledged by the foundation, and delivered to the resident agent within 30 days. The annual DGI confirmation aligns with the 31 March tax cycle; the Public Registry does not receive UBO data except through statutory or judicial request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Charter and any amendments (Escritura de Fundación)
Register of Foundation Council Members and Protector
Register of Beneficiaries and Foundation Assets
Minute Book of the Foundation Council

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 2,500 per year for a Panama licensed resident agent and registered office for a Private Interest Foundation engaged in crew-management activities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,500 per year when the audit threshold is triggered; otherwise not applicable for a dormant foundation with no Panama-source activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation excludes foreign-source revenue; PIFs deriving crew recruitment income exclusively from international voyages are outside Panama-source taxable base. Possible ITBMS (VAT) zero-rating for exported services; potential Sede de Conveniencia (Multinational Headquarters) exemptions if licensed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 201 (Declaración Jurada de Renta) filed via the Panama e-Tax 2.0 digital platform (Sistema de Información Económica, SIE)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by March 31 of the year following the fiscal year-end (standard calendar year). For off-calendar fiscal years, due by the last business day of the third month after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Panama-source gross revenue. Exclude receipts attributable to crewing services rendered for vessels operating outside Panamanian waters.
State foreign-source income explicitly exempt under Panama's territorial tax principle. Retain supporting shipping and crew contracts evidencing the extraterritorial delivery of services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after allowed deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare deductibility only of expenses incurred in generating Panama-source income. Allocate common overhead on a reasonable ratio if mixed-source income exists.
Calculate tax only on taxable Panama-source net income. If no Panama-source income, enter zero and file the nil return to maintain good standing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fine of B/ 10 plus 5% of tax due per month or fraction thereof, up to 50%. Unpaid tax is subject to monthly interest of 1%; in addition, the Comptroller General may impose a 10% surcharge for non-filing by a required taxpayer.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on distributions from Panama-source taxable profits; 0% for PIF distributions made from foreign-source or exempt income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The payee must obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence, complete DGI Form 202 (Solicitud de Aplicación de Tratado de Doble Imposición), and deliver it to the Panamanian withholding agent before the payment date. The withholding agent must keep a copy for 7 years; the DGI has 30 calendar days to approve or reject the claim.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panama imposes a 12.5% withholding tax on royalties for the use of IP (patents, trademarks, copyrights) paid to non-residents. Interest paid to unrelated non-resident lenders is subject to a 6% withholding tax; however, interest on loan agreements with Panamanian banks is exempt. Treaty rates may reduce these to 5–10% for royalties and 0–5% for interest, contingent on TRC submission and substantive economic presence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required when annual gross revenues exceed B/ 3,000,000 or related-party transactions exceed B/ 1,000,000. Master File required when consolidated gross revenue exceeds B/ 6,000,000. Penalties for non-compliance: up to B/ 50,000 plus a 5% surcharge on the recharacterized adjustment.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has not issued standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) analogous to BVI/Cayman. However, the DGI can invoke anti-abuse provisions (Arts. 760-761 Fiscal Code) and the Beneficial Ownership Law (No. 23 of 2015) to challenge shell structures. For ship crew recruitment, the entity must hold a valid SEP/CPR license and maintain real presence: a physical office in Panama, resident agent, payroll records, and vessel crew contracts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Panama-source income (e.g., crew management fees earned in Panama) from Form 201, or using fabricated deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax plus imprisonment of 2 to 5 years under Panama's Penal Tax Law (No. 14 of 2009). The DGI may also order suspension of the PIF's beneficial ownership permits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and Foundation Council members are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax. A court may issue travel bans, freeze personal accounts, and impose imprisonment against individuals who signed false declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a PIF in Panama with no office, no staff, and no substantial business activity while claiming exemption from Panamanian tax on all revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI can disregard the legal personality under Article 760, impose a 100% penalty on undeclared tax, and revoke the foundation's plumbing (permanent establishment) status. Fines can reach B/ 250,000 for repeated violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be required to pay the foundation's unpaid corporate tax from personal assets (civil liability). Flagrant abuse may trigger criminal money-laundering prosecution with a 6-year custodial sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement risk-based diligence on seafarer recruitment transactions; not filing beneficial ownership reports with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); transferring funds to sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., Iran, North Korea) without OFAC/UAF authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties under Law 23 of 2015: fines up to USD 1,000,000 per violation, plus revocation of the crew recruitment license. Criminal anti-money laundering sanctions may impose 5 to 12 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face criminal imprisonment for willful AML non-compliance. Travel bans, civil asset forfeiture, and being barred from serving as officers in Panama are automatic upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not filing the annual Beneficial Ownership Report (Form 800) to the DGI's or the registry's electronic system, or concealing the names of ultimate owners / settlor and beneficiaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of B/ 500 to B/ 2,500 per late month, and potential cancellation of the PIF's Certificate of Good Standing if the default persists for more than 90 days.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Resident Agent and Foundation Council members are jointly liable for the fine. Persistent non-compliance may result in an order for dissolution of the foundation and disqualification of the directors from acting in any Panamanian commercial entity.
